exact_statement: There exists a universal finite C such that for every n>=1, every full-dimensional isotropic log-concave probability measure mu on R^n, and every locally Lipschitz f in L^2(mu), Var_mu(f) <= C integral |grad f|^2 dmu. Isotropic means mean zero and covariance I_n. Log-concavity allows a convex extended-real potential and convex supports.
normalization: C_P is a variance-to-Dirichlet-energy constant, not its square root or the spectral gap. C_P>=1 for isotropic laws.

original_cheeger_statement: A universal c>0 satisfies h(mu)>=c/sqrt(||Cov(mu)||_op) for every full-dimensional log-concave probability law, where h is the Euclidean outer-Minkowski boundary ratio infimum over sets of mass strictly between 0 and 1. In isotropic position the bound is h(mu)>=c.
